1About this guide

You are the Responsible Person of the Business Unit (usually the head of division or director), called the Responsible Person in this guide, in the Africa CDC Results-Based Management (RBM) platform: the person named as responsible for a Business Unit (BU: a division, a unit or a directorate) in the org structure. You decide on what your Business Unit submits:

WhatSubmitted byYour decision
Specific activities of the workplanThe focal person or a staff member of your BUApprove, or reject with a reason (chapter 4)
Activity reportsAny member of your BUApprove, or reject with a reason (chapter 6)
Quarterly indicator reports of an indicator your BU contributes toYour BU, or a BU contributing to your indicatorApprove, or reject with a reason, before M&E signs off (chapter 7)

If a BU has no Responsible Person named, the Responsible Person of the Business Unit above it decides for it.

The guide follows the platform as it works on 7 November 2026. The screen captures come from the platform itself, filled with sample data: names, activities and figures are examples. Focal persons and M&E officers have their own guides.

Where to find this guide

In the platform, click User guides, the last entry of the main menu. The page lists the guide of each role: Open reads it in the browser, Download saves the PDF.

Help, at the right end of the main menu, opens this guide in a new tab on the chapter about the page you are on. On a phone it is at the top of the menu: Help on this page.

The tour

The first time you sign in, a short tour of the screen opens on your home page. Each step points at a part of the screen and says what it is for. Click Next and Back to move from step to step. Skip the tour, or the Escape key, closes it. To take it again, click your initials at the top right, then Take the tour.

2Signing in and your menu

Click Sign in with Microsoft and use your Africa CDC account, the same one as Outlook and Teams. There is no separate password for the platform.

Your menu is the menu of your Business Unit (Aggregates, Activities, Indicators), with three more items for approvers: Approve Activity Reports, Approve Indicator Reports and Review Submissions.

Top menuItemWhat it opens
DashboardThe progress of your Business Unit.
Aggregates ▾WorkplanThe workplan of your Business Unit for the selected year.
PIRSThe indicators of your Business Unit, as in the PIRS.
Project ProposalThe project proposal.
Budget OverviewThe budget codes of the broad activities of your Business Unit.
Activities ▾Broad ActivitiesThe broad activities of your Business Unit.
Specific ActivitiesThe specific activities of your Business Unit and their status. New specific opens the planning form, if you plan activities yourself.
Write Activity ReportsReport on what an activity delivered.
Approve Activity ReportsReview Submissions, tab Activity Reports (chapter 6).
Indicators ▾T3 / T4 IndicatorsThe Tier 3 and Tier 4 indicators of your Business Unit.
Write Indicator ReportThe quarterly indicator report: the result of each indicator.
Approve Indicator ReportsReview Submissions, tab Quarterly Reports (chapter 7).
Review SubmissionsEverything waiting for your decision, in four tabs (chapter 3).
Country WorkplanOnly for members of a country office.
Reporting ▾Big Tickets, the quarterly dashboard, donor reports and the Monthly Digest (chapter 9).
User guidesThe guide of each role, to read in the browser or download as PDF (chapter 1).

Two roles? If you also hold an administrator role, your pages as a Responsible Person are gathered in one dropdown called BU, next to the administration menus.

The BU and year selectors

On the right of the top bar, the BU selector chooses one of your Business Units, or All my divisions; the year selector chooses the fiscal year.

Review Submissions needs a year that has started. If the year selector reads a future year (for example FY 2027 while it is being planned), the page shows “FY2027 has not started”: click Switch to FY2026. You still see the FY2027 activities waiting for you: the Specific Activities tab lists every year.

3How submissions reach you

Emails

WhenWhat you receive
A specific activity of your Business Unit is submittedApproval needed: <activity>, with the name of the person who submitted it, the Approve and Reject buttons, and an Open in RBM button to Review Submissions.
An activity report or a quarterly indicator report of your Business Unit is submitted<Report type> submitted: <code> (<quarter> <year>), with the content of the report, the period, the author, the attachments, the Approve and Reject buttons and an Open the report button.
Reports still wait for you (every working day)<n> reports waiting for your review: each activity report and quarterly indicator report waiting for you, with its Business Unit, period and date and an Approve or reject link, and an Open Review Submissions button.
An item has waited more than 7 days for a decisionAn approval is waiting, to you and to the Responsible Person of the level above, with an Open and decide button (below).
A high-risk activity of your Business Unit starts in 14 days or lessA high-risk activity starts soon, also sent to the focal person of the activity, with an Open the activity button. Once per start date.
A budget execution import is sent to the Business Units and activities of yours are flaggedBudget execution to look at (chapter 9).
The first day of each month, if you are the Responsible Person of a directorateThe monthly digest of your directorate, with an Open the full digest button (chapter 9).

The daily reminder arrives on working days only, at most once a day, while reports wait for you. Specific activities are not in it: their email arrives once, when they are submitted. While you are out of office (chapter 8), your delegate receives a copy of these emails.

Approve or reject from the email

The emails that ask for your decision carry two buttons, Approve and Reject. Each one opens a page of the platform, Your decision, that shows the item (its type, code, title, Business Unit, year and step) and asks you to confirm. Opening the link decides nothing: only the confirm button does.

  • Approve: click Confirm approval.
  • Reject: write the Reason (sent to the author) *, then click Confirm rejection. The reason is required.
  • You can switch between Approve and Reject on the page before you confirm. Open the full page opens the item itself.
  • If you are signed out, the platform asks you to sign in, then opens the page.
  • If the item was already decided, the page says This approval is already closed and who decided it.

The decision is the same as in Review Submissions: the same rules apply and the same emails are sent.

When an approval waits more than 7 days

If an item waits for your decision for more than 7 days, the platform also opens it to the Responsible Person of the level above your Business Unit, for example the director of your directorate. Both of you receive the email An approval is waiting, with an Open and decide button. You can still decide; whoever decides first closes the step. The 7 days count from the submission, or from the decision of the step before. This happens once per approval step.

If you are the Responsible Person of the level above, the same email reaches you for the items of the Business Units below you: open it and decide, as above.

The bell

The bell in the top bar opens Your inbox. It lists what waits for you, for example “2 specific activities are awaiting your approval” or “3 reports awaiting your decision”, and refreshes every minute. Click an item to open it.

Review Submissions

Open Review Submissions in the top menu. It gathers everything waiting for your decision, for the Business Units you are responsible for, in tabs:

TabWhat it lists
Quarterly ReportsQuarterly indicator reports, one tab per quarter (chapter 7).
Activity ReportsReports on specific activities, submitted or still in draft (chapter 6).
Specific ActivitiesNew or changed specific activities waiting for approval (chapter 4).

The directorate and division filters narrow each tab. Users with the export right also see the Quarterly report Qx and Activity reports Qx buttons, which download the reports of the quarter as Excel or CSV.

4Approving specific activities

Open Review Submissions, tab Specific Activities. It lists the activities In Review of the Business Units you are responsible for, for every fiscal year: the FY column shows the year of each one, so the activities planned for next year reach you while the current year runs. Search by title, code or division.

Step 1: Read the activity

Click the eye button (View). The activity page opens with everything that was planned: details, budget and quarters, the complexity screening, the cost lines, the broad activity and the indicator it serves, and the Approval trail (chapter 5).

The complexity screening is for planning support only. It does not change the decision you make.

Step 2: Approve

Click the tick button. A dialog asks you to confirm; click Approve. The activity becomes Approved: it joins the live workplan, the Gantt chart and the dashboards, and the person who submitted it receives an email.

Or reject, with a reason

Click the cross button, write the Rejection reason * and click Confirm rejection. The reason is required. The activity becomes Rejected; the person who submitted it receives an email with your reason, and sees it in their list and in the Approval trail. They correct the activity and submit it again: it comes back to your list.

Write a reason the focal person can act on: what is missing or wrong, and what you expect instead.

Country offices. A country office plans its own activities. If you are the Responsible Person of a country office, the activities of your office reach you in the same way.

5The Approval trail

Every specific activity page ends with the section Approval trail: who did what, and when, oldest first. Focal persons, Responsible Persons, M&E and administrators see the same trail.

EventMeaning
Created as draftThe activity was first saved.
EditedSomeone saved a change. Several saves in a row by the same person show as one line.
Submitted for approvalIt was sent to you.
Approved / RejectedYour decision. A rejection shows your reason in quotes.
Edited, sent back for approvalAn approved activity was changed, so it came back to you.
CancelledThe activity was withdrawn from the workplan.

The “Waiting for” line

While the activity is In Review, the first line says whom it waits for, for example Waiting for: Responsible Person A (Responsible Person of the Business Unit). When you see your name, the decision is yours.

If the line reads Waiting for: nobody: ask your administrator to name one in Org Structure, no Responsible Person is named for the Business Unit or the ones above it. Ask the PR&A team to name one.

A changed activity comes back to you

When the focal person changes an activity you already approved, it goes back to In Review by itself. The trail shows Edited, sent back for approval, and the activity is again in your Specific Activities tab.

Editing an activity in review

The review list has no edit button: to have something changed, reject the activity with a reason and the focal person corrects it. To correct a detail yourself, open the form of the activity: in the address of the activity page, …/plan/node/<number>, replace the end by …/my-specifics/<number>/edit. Save your change: the activity stays In Review, still waiting for you, and the trail shows Edited. Then approve it.

6Approving activity reports

Open Activities › Approve Activity Reports, or Review Submissions, tab Activity Reports. The Submitted / Drafts switch chooses between reports waiting for a decision and reports still being written.

  • View Details opens the report as the author wrote it, following the Africa CDC Activity Reporting Template. It carries an Approve Report button.
  • Approve (or Approve Report on the opened report) accepts it at once. It becomes Approved and counts in the dashboards and exports.
  • Reject, from the Actions menu of the row (the opened report has no Reject button), asks for a Rejection Reason *; click Confirm Rejection. The report becomes Rejected and its author can fix it and submit it again.

The author, the focal person and the Responsible Person of the Business Unit receive an email with the decision and, for a rejection, the reason. When the report comes from a Business Unit contributing to your activity, it is reviewed by the Responsible Person of that BU first, then by you, then signed off by M&E.

7Approving quarterly indicator reports

When a quarterly indicator report needs you

Each quarter, Business Units report the result of their Tier 3 and Tier 4 indicators. The steps depend on the role of the BU on the indicator:

Report written bySteps
The main BU of the indicator (role OWNER)M&E signs it off.
A contributing BU (role CONTRIBUTOR)1. The Responsible Person of the contributing BU. 2. The Responsible Person of the main BU. 3. M&E signs it off.

Step 1: Find the report

Open Indicators › Approve Indicator Reports, or Review Submissions, tab Quarterly Reports, and pick the quarter. Two lists follow:

  • Awaiting Your Approval: your action queue. The Current Step column says which step waits, and Assigned to you marks yours.
  • All Reports: every report of your Business Units for the quarter, with its status and current step. Narrow it with the status chips (All, Draft, In review, Approved, Rejected) or tick Report expected to keep the indicators with a target this quarter.

Step 2: Open it and decide

Click the row, or Review →. The report opens with a yellow line Reviewer. You are reviewing this report and the name of your step. Read the result, the narrative, the challenges, the recommendations and the files. At the bottom:

  • Approve passes the report to the next step, or ends the review at the last one.
  • Reject asks for a reason (required) and sends the report back to its Business Unit. The focal person fixes it and submits it again.

The Workflow Timeline below shows what happened to the report and the steps still to come, with the person each one waits for.

Approving several reports at once

In Awaiting Your Approval, tick the reports assigned to you, then click Approve selected in the bar that appears. A dialog lists them; click Approve <n>. Useful at quarter close.

Report statuses

StatusWhat it means
Not startedNo report has been opened for this activity or indicator yet.
DraftStarted and saved, not yet submitted.
SubmittedSubmitted. It waits for the decision of the reviewer.
In reviewAn indicator or activity report on its way through its approval steps.
ApprovedAccepted. It now counts in the dashboards and exports.
RejectedSent back with a reason. Fix it and submit it again.
N/AMarked “not applicable”: no report is expected for this item this quarter.

8Out of office

Away on mission or on leave? Name a colleague who approves for you while you are away. Click your initials at the top right, then Out of office.

  1. Under New delegation, choose the Delegate *: type a name to find the colleague.
  2. Choose the First day * and the Last day *. A delegation lasts at most 60 days.
  3. Add a Reason if you wish (mission, leave), then click Save the delegation.

From the first to the last day, your delegate can approve or reject what waits for you, and sees it in their Review Submissions. They also receive a copy of your platform emails. You can still decide yourself.

  • Your delegations lists the delegations you planned. End, then Confirm end, stops one before its last day.
  • Delegated to you lists the colleagues who named you. While their delegation runs, what waits for them reaches you too.
  • Two delegations cannot cover the same days: the message A delegation already covers these dates: end it first asks you to end the first one.
  • The delegate must be an active user, and not yourself. A delegate cannot pass the delegation on.

9Budget execution and the monthly digest

Budget execution to look at

After each budget execution import sent to the Business Units, the platform checks every broad activity that has a released budget, using the figures of the import. Two flags can appear:

FlagWhen
Over budgetMore committed and spent than released: committed plus spent is above the released budget of the broad activity.
Slow executionFrom the third quarter only: the broad activity has used much less than the time passed, more than 30 points behind (for example less than 20 % used when half of the year has passed).

Each Business Unit with flagged activities receives one email, Budget execution to look at, sent to its focal person and its Responsible Person. It gives the date of the budget execution figures and lists the flagged broad activities, with their execution rate and released budget. It is sent once per import.

On the Dashboard, the Budget execution block shows the same flag next to the title of the activity, in the table of activities. Point at the flag to read the reason. Click the activity to open the broad activity and its budget lines.

The monthly digest

On the first day of each month, the Responsible Person of each directorate receives the monthly digest of the directorate by email, with an Open the full digest button. The same page is in the menu: Reporting › Monthly Digest. It covers the directorate and every Business Unit under it.

SectionWhat it shows
Specific activities <year>The specific activities of the year, counted by status.
Waiting more than 7 days for a decisionSpecific activities, activity reports and quarterly indicator reports still waiting for a decision after 7 days, oldest first, with the date they wait since.
High-risk activitiesThe activities marked High risk, with their start date.
Activity reports <quarter>The activity reports of the reporting quarter by status, and how many activities were declared not started.
Indicator reports <quarter>The T3/T4 indicators owned by these Business Units, and their quarterly indicator reports by status.
Budget execution (figures as at …)The execution rate of each Business Unit from the latest import, and the number of activities to look at.

The page shows the situation on the day you open it. Print or save as PDF prints it on A4; in the print window, choose to save as PDF to keep a copy. Click a code to open the activity.

The digest is for the Responsible Person of a directorate and, while it runs, their out-of-office delegate. A Responsible Person of a division alone sees No digest for you.

Statuses of a specific activity

StatusWhat it means
DraftSaved but not submitted. Drafts stay private until you submit. Everything can still change.
In ReviewSubmitted. The Responsible Person of the Business Unit decides. It cannot be edited from the list while it waits.
ApprovedPart of the workplan of the Business Unit. It shows in the Workplan and, if its place is a country with a country office, in the Country Workplan.
RejectedSent back with a reason. Edit it and submit it again.
CancelledWithdrawn from the workplan. It stays in the list for the record.

Good practice

  • Decide within a few working days: the focal person cannot report on an activity until it is approved. After 7 days, the item is also opened to the Responsible Person of the level above.
  • Always give a reason the focal person can act on when you reject.
  • For changes to broad activities, indicators, targets or the reporting timeline, contact the PR&A team.

Need help? Contact the PR&A team for the plan and the org structure, and the Software Developer Unit for the platform. This guide reflects the platform on 7 November 2026.
